bib.title: PromptChainer: Chaining Large Language Model Prompts through Visual Programming

question: What do users need when authoring their own LLM chains, and can a visual programming interface support that?
contributions: Formative analysis of three LLM chain authoring challenges
PromptChainer, a visual interface for building and debugging LLM chains
Case studies with four designers and developers

method.summary: A node-edge visual chain editor (Chain View, Node View) with LLM, helper and communication nodes, auto-synced prompt placeholders as function signatures, and unit, end-to-end and breakpoint debugging. Evaluated qualitatively with four Google participants building their own chains.
method.task: authoring and debugging multi-step LLM prompt chains

inference.samples: not stated; one session per participant
inference.prompting: zero-shot and few-shot prompts with [[placeholder]] templates; participants drafted their own prompts

metrics.name: qualitative observation
metrics.definition: think-aloud sessions, transcribed comments, node-type counts

eval.protocol: 4 participants (3 designers, 1 developer, Google); 30 min preparation (10-min tutorial plus drafting prompts), hour-long session, about 90 min total, $75 gift credit; qualitative analysis, no statistics

prompts.text: [Dialog] Play some music I like. [Class] is_music [Dialog] hey there, what's up [Class]

results.claim: All four participants built their desired chains in the session.
results.setup: User study, 4 participants, LaMDA 137B, own application ideas
results.quote: with the chains containing on average 5.5 ± 0.9 nodes

results.claim: Participants used three times as many pre-defined helper nodes as custom JS nodes.
results.setup: Node counts over user study chains and pilot chains (8 chains total)
results.quote: participants used three times as many pre-defined helpers (13 in total) as customized JS nodes (4)

results.claim: Of 27 LLM nodes, 7 categorize inputs, 13 source information from the LLM, 7 re-organize input.
results.setup: One author coded LLM nodes by primitive LLM operations of Wu et al. 2022 (AI Chains)
results.quote: out of the 27 LLM nodes, 7 were for categorizing inputs, 13 for sourcing information from the LLM, and 7 for re-organizing the input

results.claim: Independently generated parallel paragraphs reduced coherence in a story chain.

limits: Only four participants, all at Google, qualitative only
Participants pre-drafted prompts, which may have anchored them to their decomposition
Tasks may have been naturally easy to decompose
Coherence across interdependent parallel sub-tasks and tracing complex chains remain open
Short extended abstract: no quantitative comparison against a baseline tool

terms.definition: decomposing an overarching task into a series of highly targeted sub-tasks, mapping each to a distinct LLM step, and using the output from one step as an input to the next

lineage.work: AI Chains: Transparent and Controllable Human-AI Interaction by Chaining Large Language Model Prompts
lineage.note: proposed chaining; this work studies authoring

lineage.work: Prompt-based Prototyping with Large Language Models
LaMDA: Language Models for Dialog Applications
